style: Say playfully and cheerfully, like a fun music teacher
lines: Tap a block on the shelf, then tap a space in the song strip. Then press Play song.
Press Play song to hear your form.
Tap the grid to change the notes. Every copy of this section changes too.
Tap beats 7 and 8 to give the twin its own ending. Beats 1 to 6 follow its parent.
You changed A, so every A changed. Same letter, same music.
You changed B, so every B changed. Same letter, same music.
You changed C, so every C changed. Same letter, same music.
You changed D, so every D changed. Same letter, same music.
A prime starts as a copy. Change its last two beats to make a twin.
B prime starts as a copy. Change its last two beats to make a twin.
C prime starts as a copy. Change its last two beats to make a twin.
The same music every time. That's how verses work.
A and its twin. Same start, new ending.
Nothing came back. Every part was new.
A B. Two parts.
A A B B. Each part says itself twice.
A B A. You went away and came back home.
A A B A. Lots of songs use this shape.
A rondo! A keeps coming back between other parts.
That shape has no special name, and that's okay.
Two of your sections have the same notes. Change one so it sounds new.
Put a block in the song strip first.
Press Listen. Then tap Same, Almost the same, or New for each part.
Listen again. Is it exactly the same, a little different, or new?
Exactly the same music: the same letter again.
Same start, different ending: a twin.
New music: a new letter.
Yes! The same music again.
Yes! Same start, new ending.
Yes! New music.
Hot Cross Buns is A A B A. B is a quick trip away, and A brings you home.
Mary Had a Little Lamb is A A prime. Its new ending is what makes it sound finished.
Twinkle Twinkle is A B A. The tune comes home at the end, so it feels finished.
Ode to Joy is A A prime B A prime. B is the trip away, and A prime brings you back.
Row Row Row Your Boat is A B C D. Nothing comes back, so it feels like a trip down the river.
Frere Jacques is A A B B C C D D. Every part says itself twice, so it is easy to remember.
Now tap a space in the song strip to put your block there.
Now tap a block in the song strip to swap in your block.
Tap Hear or Remove under the strip. Or tap a shelf block, then this space, to swap it.
Tap Hear, Make it A prime, or Remove under the strip. Or tap a shelf block, then this space, to swap it.
Tap Hear, Make it B prime, or Remove under the strip. Or tap a shelf block, then this space, to swap it.
Tap Hear, Make it C prime, or Remove under the strip. Or tap a shelf block, then this space, to swap it.
Your twin is still a copy. Tap Edit on its shelf block and change beats 7 and 8.
Press Play song to hear your form. Or tap a shelf block to add more.
Tap Edit on a shelf block to change its notes. Then press Play song again.
The strip is full. Press Play song, or tap a block in the strip to remove it.
Listen for the parts that come back. Press Stop to stop.
Listen to this section. Press Stop to stop.
Tap the grid to change the notes. Every copy changes too. Press Done when you are finished.
Tap the grid in beats 7 and 8 to give the twin its own ending. Press Done when you are finished.
Clear your whole song, notes and all? Tap Yes or No.
Load this starter song in place of yours? Tap Yes or No.
Listen to the music. Press Stop to stop.
Here is the answer. Then the next part plays. Press Stop to pause.
Listen to the two parts, one after the other. Then tap Same, Almost, or New.
Start this song over? Your labels go away. Tap Yes or No.
Is this part the same, almost the same, or new? Tap a Same, Almost, or New button, or Hear it again.
Listen again. Is it exactly the same, a little different, or new? Tap Same, Almost, or New.
Press Play whole song to hear the form. Or pick another song.
